findings.observation: Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) was reviewed using the vision tool. The sheet shows adjacent properties labeled with both zoning designations (CS, CS-V, CS-MU-V-CO, SF-3, P) and actual land uses (e.g., 'USE: OFFICE', 'USE: APARTMENT/CONDO', 'USE: COMMERCIAL', 'USE: GOVERNMENT SERVICES', 'USE: SINGLE-FAMILY'). The land use information is integrated directly into the main site plan drawing, showing properties to the north, east, south, and west of the proposed development. The plan clearly identifies the SF-3 zoned property to the west as single-family use, and shows other adjacent uses including apartments/condos, commercial, office, and government services.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a 'land use map showing adjacent land uses' when subject to Compatibility Standards. The site is confirmed to be subject to Compatibility Standards (CS-V zoning within 75 feet of SF-3 triggering property, per CC Application Section 10 and facts.md). Sheet 13 provides this required land use map by showing both zoning and actual land uses for all adjacent properties. While there is no separate standalone 'land use map' section, the integrated presentation on the site plan satisfies the requirement by clearly depicting adjacent land uses in relation to the proposed development, which is the regulatory intent.
findings.explanation: Sheet 13 shows adjacent properties with both zoning designations and land uses clearly labeled (office, commercial, apartment/condo, single-family).

findings.observation: Sheets 35 and 36 (Building Elevations) were reviewed using the vision tool. Sheet 35 shows North and East elevations; Sheet 36 shows South and West elevations. All four elevations display comprehensive architectural elements including: windows (both punched windows on upper floors and storefront glazing at ground level), doors and entrance areas, projecting and recessed balconies with railings, material finishes (fiber cement board painted, king brick, wood tone fiber cement, glass, living wall), rooflines with flat roofs and varying parapet heights, and vertical articulation through material changes and facade planes. Both sheets include a Material Legend clearly identifying all exterior finishes. Floor levels (Level 1 through Level 6 and Roof) are explicitly marked on all elevations with elevation callouts.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 'building elevations showing architectural elements' when subject to Compatibility Standards. Sheets 35-36 provide all four building elevations (North, East, South, West) with detailed architectural elements that demonstrate the building's design, massing, vertical articulation, and material palette. The elevations include windows, doors, balconies, material finishes, rooflines, and floor levels - all of which are essential architectural elements required to evaluate compatibility with adjacent residential uses. The material legend on both sheets clearly identifies five distinct exterior materials. This level of detail satisfies the completeness check requirement for building elevations showing architectural elements.
findings.explanation: Sheets 35-36 show all four building elevations (North, East, South, West) with detailed architectural elements including windows, balconies, materials, and rooflines.

findings.observation: Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 of 2) was reviewed using the vision tool. The sheet shows compatibility setback lines both graphically on the site plan and in a table. The graphically depicted setback lines include: 15' Compatibility Setback Line, 25' Compatibility Setback Line, 50' Compatibility Setback Line, and 75' Compatibility Setback Line, all drawn as dashed lines parallel to the southern and southwestern property boundaries adjacent to the SF-3 zoned single-family property (Kinney Avenue Bungalows). The table titled 'COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINES' shows allowable building heights at different distances: 0'-10' (0' height, screening zone), 10'-25' (0' height, restricted zone), 25'-50' (40' height), and 50'-75' (60' height). The proposed building footprint is shown positioned outside the restricted zones, demonstrating compliance with the setback requirements.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires that 'setbacks adjacent to residential uses or zoning' be shown on plans when subject to Compatibility Standards. Sheet 14 satisfies this requirement by showing the compatibility setbacks in two complementary ways: (1) graphically on the site plan as labeled dashed lines at 15', 25', 50', and 75' distances from the property line adjacent to the SF-3 residential property, and (2) in a table that defines the allowable building heights within each zone. The combination of graphic depiction and tabular specification clearly demonstrates the setback relationship between the proposed building and the adjacent residential property to the west. This presentation allows reviewers to verify that the building design respects the compatibility setback requirements.
findings.explanation: Sheet 14 shows compatibility setback lines both graphically (15', 25', 50', 75' lines) and in a table with allowable heights adjacent to SF-3 residential zoning.

summary: All 3 checklist items pass. The site plan includes a land use map showing adjacent uses (Sheet 13), building elevations showing architectural elements (Sheets 35-36), and compatibility setbacks adjacent to residential zoning (Sheet 14).
